source.title: Finite Versus Infinite Neural Networks: an Empirical Study
source.authors: Jaehoon Lee; S. Schoenholz; Jeffrey Pennington; Ben Adlam; Lechao Xiao; Roman Novak; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary material, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports test accuracy across architectures and network widths on natural image labels, using a different setup from the claim versions. It does not test random-label memorization or the specified one-hidden-layer width setting.
record.gate_note: Results about random labels and cited prior-work results are not this study's own tests. The paper reports CIFAR-10 accuracy for finite networks across architectures and widths; its batch-size discussion concerns training dynamics, not the test-error comparison in V5.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own width sweeps and convolutional-versus-fully-connected accuracy comparisons on CIFAR-10. These bear on V2 and V3 in new architecture and training settings; it is not an original source for either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate but understates the central finite-versus-infinite comparison. Kernels outperform base finite FCN and CNN-VEC, while finite CNN-GAP outperforms its kernels; ensembling and training interventions alter these relationships. Width generally improves accuracy, with an intermediate optimum for NTK-parameterized CNN-VEC. The authors also find that exploiting equivariance depends on leaving the kernel regime.
record.recipe_differences: Studies finite versus infinite network behavior on natural CIFAR-10 labels using MSE, mini-batch SGD, architecture and width sweeps, and training interventions; it does not test random-label fitting or the claim's exact models and recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and parameterization affect performance; width dependence is non-monotonic for CNN-VEC with NTK parameterization. Training interventions such as L2, large learning rates, early stopping, and ensembling also change reported accuracy, but are not the width sweep's isolated comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Finite-versus-kernel comparisons depend on architecture, and ensembling can close or reverse their performance differences.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether infinite-width kernel predictors match finite-network accuracy depends on architecture and training procedure.

record.problems: The study does not report random-label results. Width-sweep values are shown in figures without exact numbers in the text, and the width analysis uses deep architectures on CIFAR-10 rather than the specific one-hidden-layer setup in V2. The reported architecture comparison does not isolate local connectivity from other architectural differences such as pooling.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results on the tested versions were omitted. Other Table S1 intervention results concern training procedures, but do not directly test the named claim versions beyond the base architecture comparison.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting or natural-versus-random-label held-out comparison.

The original one-hidden-layer, unregularized MNIST/downsampled-CIFAR-10 recipe and interpolation-threshold behavior are not tested. Training termination uses greater than 99% accuracy on a 5,000-example training subset, rather than establishing zero full-training error at each width. Regularized and early-stopped curves do not establish the unregularized convergence claim.

No controlled isolation of local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, or initialization from trained convolutional networks. No corresponding finite-network architecture comparison on MNIST, CIFAR-100, or SVHN.
Batch-size curves use training steps, not a matched fixed-epoch held-out comparison.
No dropout intervention or joint dropout-and-weight-decay removal.
No magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization-gap evaluation.
No removal and retraining comparison for memorized versus random examples.

missing.what: Cross-entropy architecture comparisons: base FCN/CNN-VEC/CNN-GAP accuracies are 55.01/64.31/83.66% in STD and 53.39/67.13/83.87% in NTK parameterization. These extend the recorded MSE comparison to a standard classification loss.

record.verdict_notes: Verdicts use only the supplied text. Architecture comparisons establish accuracy differences without identifying their causal component. Width verdicts rely on the authors' explicit interpretation in §3.6; aggregated rows cannot establish the behavior of every individual recipe.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not fit random labels or compare held-out accuracy on random versus natural labels.
Uses deep FCN/CNN architectures on CIFAR-10, not one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10; the figure does not specify a zero-training-error threshold for every width.

Tests FCN against CNN-VEC and CNN-GAP on CIFAR-10, but not MNIST, CIFAR-100, or SVHN; it does not test fully connected networks learning sparse local connections or convolutional initialization transfer.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers against SGD or momentum SGD.
Batch size is discussed through training dynamics; the paper does not report the fixed-epoch held-out performance comparison in this version.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison of generalization measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

relationships.condition: Base finite networks trained from scratch with MSE and mini-batch SGD, both parameterizations
relationships.reason: R1–R6 show CNN-VEC/CNN-GAP accuracy of 56.68/80.26% versus FCN 47.82% in STD, and 60.73/80.61% versus 46.16% in NTK parameterization.
relationships.display_finding: Under standard (STD) parameterization, accuracy was 56.68% for the CNN with vectorized outputs (CNN-VEC), 80.26% for the CNN with global average pooling (CNN-GAP), and 47.82% for the fully connected network (FCN). Under neural tangent kernel (NTK) parameterization, accuracies were 60.73% for CNN-VEC, 80.61% for CNN-GAP and 46.16% for FCN.
